correctness.rationale: For all fields K, r>=1 and A=Sym(V)/(V)^3 with V=m/m² and W=Sym²(V), a scalar-fixing endomorphism f on generators is uniquely (P,Q), P:V→V and Q:V→W. Degree-two map is Sym²(P), so f²=f iff P²=P and Q=QP+Sym²(P)Q. For V=U⊕T, U=im P dim k, constraints Q(U) lies in ker Sym²(P) of dimension s-s_k and Q(T) lies in Sym²U of dimension s_k. Thus each rank-k linear projection has q^[k(s-s_k)+(r-k)s_k] quadratic lifts. Grassmannian k-plane U choices {r choose k}_q and q^[k(r-k)] complements produce I_{r,k}={r choose k}_q q^[k(r-k)+d_(r,k)]. Distinct image algebras correspond one-to-one to graph maps U→W/Sym²U, giving R_{r,k}={r choose k}_q q^[k(s-s_k)] and q^[(r-k)(k+s_k)] lifts per image. These arguments use ordinary symmetric powers without division by 2, so hold in characteristic 2 and at endpoints k=0,r; bundle geometry follows by constant-rank linear constraints. Independent full endomorphism P/Q enumeration yields r=2,q=2: 48 middle-rank maps/12 images; q=3: 324/36, with one map/image in rank 0 and full rank. The finite counts are corroboration only.

None supplies an all-endomorphism classification for the cubic nilpotent quotient, the separate embedded-image counts, or finite-field Gaussian fiber multiplicities. The Artinian cube-zero algebra and its retract space are natural, while a possible equivalent jet-algebra/coordinate-change classification remains a bibliographic risk.

value.rationale: The cube-zero full symmetric truncation is a canonical finite-dimensional local commutative algebra. A complete description of its idempotent endomorphisms and embedded retracts (distinct objects), Gaussian q-counts, per-image multiplicities and irreducible smooth moduli are exact natural invariants, potentially useful in deformation and finite ring studies. The two distinct enumerators contain nontrivial information beyond merely identifying coordinate projection examples.

limitations: All fields for structural classification and finite F_q for counts; unital K-algebra maps and m³ truncation only.
Numerical check r=2 over prime fields does not establish all r and prime powers; algebraic proof does.
